_meta.source: Private ABE review compilation notes (2025), TRANSES collection
_meta.extraction_method: Manually transcribed by reading rendered page images against the source PDF, page by page, formulas only — not tables/constants (separate future pass).
_meta.status: draft — not yet spot-checked by a second human reviewer; ready for DB import as status=draft, promote to published after review
topic_mapping_notes: "Engineering Economy Transes.pdf" mapped directly to the existing topic "Engineering Economy and Project Feasibility Analysis" (PROJECT_MGMT_RDE) — clean subject match.

"Machinery and Mechanization Transes.pdf" mapped directly to the existing topic "Farm Machinery and Mechanization, Economics, Management, and Marketing" (POWER_ENERGY_MACHINERY) — its formula content (tillage/planter calibration, actual field capacity, sprayer calibration, farm pump sizing, tractor power-transmission ratios) is squarely machinery-management math.

"Marketing and Management Transes.pdf" turned out to be general business/marketing/management theory (management functions, leadership styles, market structure, financial ratios) rather than farm-machinery-specific content, so it did not fit the existing "Farm Machinery..." topic well. Created a new topic "Marketing and Management" under PROJECT_MGMT_RDE (project/enterprise financial and business-management math). Only 4 genuine formulas existed in this source — the rest of the file is definitional/list content with no formula, out of scope for this pass.
"Surveying Transes.pdf" mapped directly to the existing topic "Surveying" (LAND_WATER) — clean subject match.

In the Machinery source's 'Actual Field Capacity' box (page 9), one line ('Number of rows = W/upland, L/upland') was ambiguous/illegible in the source image and was omitted rather than guessed at, per the no-fabrication instruction; the rest of that formula box (Total area, T1, T2, Total time, AFC) was transcribed as printed.
_meta.privacy_note: Source material's own attribution/branding (present on every page footer) intentionally NOT carried into any field, per explicit instruction — source is recorded generically only.

topics.topic_name: Engineering Economy and Project Feasibility Analysis

entries.title: Simple Interest
entries.variables: I = interest, P = principal/present worth, i = interest rate per period, n = number of interest periods, F = accumulated/future amount
entries.description: Interest computed on the principal only, ignoring any interest accrued in prior periods.

entries.title: Compound Interest — Discrete Compounding
entries.variables: F = future worth, P = present worth, i = interest rate per period, n = number of periods
entries.description: Interest is compounded at the end of each finite-length period (month, quarter, year).

entries.title: Compound Interest — Continuous Compounding
entries.variables: F = future worth, P = present worth, r = nominal annual interest rate, n = number of years
entries.description: Cash payments are assumed to occur once a year, but compounding is continuous throughout the year.

entries.title: Nominal Rate of Interest
entries.variables: r = nominal annual interest rate, m = number of compounding periods per year, n = number of years, i = rate per compounding period
entries.description: Specifies the interest rate and number of compounding periods within one year.

entries.title: Effective Rate of Interest
entries.variables: i = nominal rate per period, m = number of compounding periods per year, r = continuous nominal rate
entries.description: The actual/exact interest rate earned on the principal during one full year.

entries.title: Discount Rate
entries.variables: d = discount rate, i = interest rate
entries.description: Relates the discount rate (a rate applied against future value) to the equivalent interest rate.

entries.title: Inflation Rate
entries.variables: i_f = inflated interest rate, i = real interest rate, f = inflation rate
entries.description: Adjusts an interest rate to account for a given rate of inflation.

entries.title: Uniform Series Present Worth (P/A, i, n)
entries.variables: P = present worth, A = uniform periodic payment, i = interest rate per period, n = number of periods
entries.description: Converts a uniform series of future payments (ordinary annuity) into its present worth.

entries.title: Capital Recovery (A/P, i, n)
entries.variables: A = uniform periodic payment, P = present worth, i = interest rate per period, n = number of periods
entries.description: Converts a present value into a series of equal periodic payments.

entries.title: Uniform Series Compound Amount (F/A, i, n)
entries.variables: F = future worth, A = uniform periodic payment, i = interest rate per period, n = number of periods
entries.description: Converts a series of equal periodic payments into its future value.

entries.title: Sinking Fund (A/F, i, n)
entries.variables: A = uniform periodic payment, F = future worth, i = interest rate per period, n = number of periods
entries.description: Finds the equal periodic payments needed to accumulate a given future amount.

entries.title: Present Value
entries.variables: PV = present value, FV = future value, i = interest/discount rate, n = number of periods
entries.description: Money now is more valuable than money later; discounts a future amount to today's value.

entries.title: Benefit/Cost Ratio (BCR)
entries.variables: Benefits = advantages to owners/public, Disbenefits = expected negative consequences, Cost = estimated project expenditures
entries.description: Ratio of present value of benefits to present value of costs; project is economically justified if BCR > 1.

entries.title: Break-Even Analysis (One Decision Variable)
entries.formula: R = C_T        R = pD        C_T = VC_T + FC        VC_T = (VC)(D)
entries.variables: R = revenue, C_T = total cost, p = unit price, D = quantity of units, VC_T = total variable cost, FC = fixed cost, VC = variable cost per unit
entries.description: Level of production/output where total income equals total expense.

entries.title: Break-Even Quantity
entries.variables: D_BEP = break-even quantity sold, FC = total fixed cost, p = unit price, VC = variable cost per unit
entries.description: Quantity that must be sold for revenue to equal total cost.

entries.title: Return on Investment (ROI)
entries.variables: Net Profit = profit earned, Total Investment = investor's cost basis
entries.description: Financial ratio measuring the benefit an investor receives relative to investment cost.

entries.title: Profit and Revenue Maximization
entries.formula: P = a − bD        D* = (a − VC)/2b   (demand maximizing profit)        D' = a/2b   (demand maximizing revenue)
entries.variables: P = unit price, a, b = demand-function coefficients, D = demand/quantity, VC = variable cost per unit
entries.description: Finds the demand level that maximizes profit or revenue given a linear price-demand relationship.

entries.title: Depreciation — Straight-Line Method
entries.formula: d = (C_o − C_n)/n        D_m = md = (C_o − C_n)(m/n)        C_m = C_o − D_m
entries.variables: C_o = original/first cost, C_n = book value at end of life (salvage/scrap value), n = useful life in years, m = age of property at any time ≤ n, d = annual depreciation cost, D_m = accrued depreciation up to m years, C_m = book value at end of m years
entries.description: Loss in value is directly proportional to the age of the asset; gives a uniform annual depreciation charge.

entries.title: Depreciation — Sinking Fund Method
entries.variables: C_o = original cost, C_n = book value at end of life, n = useful life, m = age of property, i = interest rate, d = annual cost of depreciation, D_m = accrued depreciation to m years, C_m = book value at m years
entries.description: Funds are set aside annually (earning interest via a sinking fund) to accumulate the cost of replacing the asset at the end of its useful life.

entries.title: Depreciation — Declining Balance Method (Matheson Formula)
entries.formula: k = 1 − ᵐ√(C_m/C_o) = 1 − ⁿ√(C_n/C_o)        d_m = kC_(m−1)        C_m = C_o(1 − k)^m        C_n = C_o(1 − k)^n
entries.variables: k = constant percentage rate of depreciation, C_o = original cost, C_m = book value at m years, C_n = book value at end of life n, d_m = depreciation charge at year m
entries.description: Annual depreciation cost is a fixed percentage of the book value at the beginning of the year (accelerated/constant-percentage method).

entries.title: Depreciation — Sum-of-Years'-Digits (SYD) Method
entries.formula: SYD = n(n+1)/2        D = (remaining useful life / SYD) × (Depreciable Basis)
entries.variables: n = useful life, SYD = sum of the years' digits, D = depreciation charge for the year
entries.description: Accelerated depreciation method producing higher charges in early years and lower charges later in the asset's life.

topics.topic_name: Farm Machinery and Mechanization, Economics, Management, and Marketing

entries.title: Draft Horsepower (DHP)
entries.variables: F = draft/force required, S = travel speed
entries.description: Power required to pull an implement (e.g., a disc plow) through the soil.

entries.title: Swath (Plowing)
entries.variables: n = number of rounds
entries.description: Effective width of area covered by the plow/implement in one pass, for round-about/gathering plowing.

entries.title: Disc Angle
entries.variables: Swath = effective working width, Diameter = disc diameter
entries.description: Angle the disc makes with the direction of travel, calculated from the swath and disc diameter.

entries.title: Width of Disk Harrow (by type)
entries.formula: Tandem: W = 0.95NS + 1.2D        Offset: W = 0.95NS + 0.6D        Single-action: W = 0.95NS + 0.3D        Double offset: W = 0.95NS + 0.85D
entries.variables: N = number of disks, S = disk spacing, D = disk diameter
entries.description: Estimates the effective working width of a disc harrow based on its configuration.

entries.title: Expected Plant Population (EPP)
entries.formula: EPP = [(10,000 m²/ha)(seeds per hill)(emergence)] / (Row Spacing × Hill Spacing)
entries.variables: Row Spacing, Hill Spacing = planter geometry, emergence = fraction of seeds expected to emerge
entries.description: Predicted number of plants per hectare for a planter calibration, before accounting for the seed metering device.

entries.title: Expected Plant Population — With Seed Plate (Groundwheel-Driven)
entries.formula: EPP (plants/ha) = [(10,000 m²/ha)(seeds per hill)(seed plate)(emergence)] / (Row Spacing × Hill Spacing)
entries.variables: seed plate = seed-plate metering factor, Row Spacing, Hill Spacing = planter geometry, emergence = fraction of seeds expected to emerge
entries.description: Expected plant population accounting for the seed-plate metering device on a groundwheel-driven planter.

entries.title: Hill Spacing (HS) — Given Groundwheel/Sprocket Ratio
entries.variables: D = groundwheel diameter, SR = sprocket/speed ratio
entries.description: Planter hill spacing computed from the groundwheel diameter and drive sprocket ratio.

entries.title: Hill Spacing (HS) — Given Gear Teeth
entries.formula: HS = [(circumference of groundwheel)(T4/T3 × T2/T1)] / seed plate
entries.variables: T1–T4 = number of teeth on each gear in the drive train, seed plate = seed-plate metering factor
entries.description: Planter hill spacing computed from the groundwheel circumference and the gear-teeth ratios of the drive train.

entries.title: Planter Seeding Adjustment
entries.formula: Area (covered by groundwheel) = Width × Distance        Width = Rows × Row length        Distance = πD × No. of rev
entries.variables: D = groundwheel diameter, No. of rev = number of groundwheel revolutions
entries.description: Area covered by the groundwheel during a calibration run, used to adjust seeding rate.

entries.title: Adjusted Seed Setting
entries.formula: Adjusted seed setting = Discharge setting × (10,000 m² / Area)
entries.variables: Discharge setting = seed discharged at the tested setting, Area = area covered per the seeding-adjustment formula
entries.description: Corrects a planter's seed-rate dial setting to achieve the target per-hectare rate.

entries.title: Actual Field Capacity (AFC)
entries.formula: Total area = W × L        T1 (time to turn) = (# of rows) × (seconds/row)        T2 (time to cover length) = (L × # of rows) / speed        Total time = T1 + T2        AFC = Total Area / Total Time
entries.variables: W = plot width, L = plot length, T1 = turning time, T2 = time to cover length
entries.description: Actual field capacity of a machine/implement accounting for turning time and travel time over a plot.

entries.title: Animal-Drawn Weeder Performance Index
entries.variables: FC = field capacity, %Damage and Eff = not expressed as decimals, Power = rated at 1 hp per animal
entries.description: Rates the performance of an animal-drawn weeder based on field capacity, plant damage, and efficiency.

entries.title: Sprayer Field Capacity (FC)
entries.variables: S = speed (kph), W = effective swath (m), Eff = field efficiency (not decimal)
entries.description: Effective field capacity of a boom/knapsack sprayer.

entries.title: Sprayer Pump Capacity (Q)
entries.formula: Pump capacity (Q) = Application rate × Swath × Speed        Pump capacity (Q) = Application rate × FC
entries.variables: Application rate = target spray volume per hectare, Swath = effective spray width, Speed = travel speed, FC = field capacity
entries.description: Required pump discharge to deliver a target spray application rate.

entries.title: Volume of Water Applied (Sprayer)
entries.variables: Nozzle Discharge = flow rate from the nozzle, Swath = effective spray width, Speed = travel speed
entries.description: Actual spray volume applied per hectare, from measured nozzle discharge, swath, and travel speed.

entries.title: Amount of Chemical to Mix with Water
entries.formula: Amount (kg) = [(Swath)(Speed)(Capacity of Tank)(Chemical app. rate)] / [(Q)(10,000 m²/ha)]
entries.variables: Q = pump capacity, Capacity of Tank = sprayer tank volume, Chemical app. rate = target chemical application rate
entries.description: Quantity of chemical concentrate to mix into a sprayer tank to achieve the target application rate.

entries.title: Atmospheric Pressure — Rise of Water in a Tube
entries.variables: h = rise of water in the tube, P = atmospheric pressure, ρ = specific weight of water
entries.description: Height to which atmospheric pressure alone can theoretically raise water in a suction tube (basis for pump suction-lift limits).

entries.title: Pump Output Power
entries.variables: Q = discharge (gpm), H = head (ft), Eff = pump efficiency
entries.description: Hydraulic output power delivered by a water pump.

entries.title: Pump Input (Electrical) Power
entries.variables: I = current (Amps), V = voltage (Volts)
entries.description: Electrical power drawn by an electric-motor-driven pump.

entries.title: Pump Efficiency
entries.variables: Output = hydraulic output power, Input = shaft/electrical input power
entries.description: Ratio of a pump's useful output power to its input power.

entries.title: Tractor Drive Wheel % Slippage — Speed-Based
entries.variables: N_underload = wheel rotational speed under load, N_no load = wheel rotational speed with no load
entries.description: Percent wheel slip computed from rotational speed under load versus no-load.

entries.title: Tractor Drive Wheel % Slippage — Distance-Based
entries.variables: D_actual = actual distance traveled per given wheel revolutions, D_theoretical = theoretical distance for the same revolutions
entries.description: Percent wheel slip computed from actual versus theoretical travel distance.

entries.title: Length of Flat or V-Belt
entries.variables: C = center-to-center distance between shafts, D1 = diameter of larger pulley, D2 = diameter of smaller pulley
entries.description: Required belt length for an open (flat or V) belt drive.

entries.title: Length of Cross Belt
entries.variables: C = center-to-center distance between shafts, D1 = diameter of larger pulley, D2 = diameter of smaller pulley
entries.description: Required belt length for a crossed belt drive.

entries.title: Belt-Pulley Speed Ratio
entries.variables: N1, N2 = rotational speeds of driver/driven pulleys, D1, D2 = their diameters
entries.description: Speed relationship between two pulleys connected by a belt (driven pulley speed decreases as its diameter increases).

entries.title: Chain-Sprocket Speed Ratio
entries.variables: N1, N2 = rotational speeds of the two sprockets, T1, T2 = number of teeth on each sprocket
entries.description: Speed relationship between two sprockets connected by a roller chain.

entries.title: Gear System Speed Ratio
entries.variables: N_driven = rotational speed of driven gear, N_driver = rotational speed of driver gear
entries.description: Speed relationship between two meshed gears (rotation direction is reversed between them).

entries.title: Tractor Linear (Ground) Speed and Speed Ratios
entries.formula: V = 2πN7 = πDN7        Speed Ratios = N_engine/N_groundwheel        V = πDN        Speed Ratios = V_engine/V_tractor
entries.variables: D = groundwheel/wheel diameter, N = rotational speed, N7 = groundwheel rpm, V = linear speed
entries.description: Relates tractor ground speed to groundwheel rotation and to the overall engine-to-tractor speed ratio.

entries.title: Tractor Drivetrain Speed-Reduction Train
entries.formula: N1D1 = N2D2        N2 = N3        N3T3 = N4T4        N4 = N5        N5T5 = N6T6        N6 = N7 (Rev. of ground wheel)
entries.variables: N1–N7 = rotational speeds at successive stages of the drivetrain, D1, D2 = pulley diameters, T3–T6 = gear/sprocket teeth counts
entries.description: Chain of belt, gear, and chain speed reductions from engine shaft down to the tractor's ground wheel.

entries.title: Current Ratio (Liquidity/Solvency)
entries.formula: Current Ratio = Current Assets / Current Liabilities
entries.variables: Ideal current ratio ≥ 2:1
entries.description: Measures a company's ability to cover its short-term liabilities with its short-term assets.

entries.title: Quick / Acid-Test Ratio
entries.variables: Ideal ratio ≥ 1:1
entries.description: Shows whether a company can pay short-term obligations using only cash and assets quickly convertible to cash (excludes inventory).

entries.title: Net Working Capital (NWC)
entries.description: Represents the amount of funds available for day-to-day operations.

entries.title: Customer Value
entries.variables: Benefits = what the customer gets from a product, Costs = money, time, and effort paid
entries.description: The perceived net gain a customer receives from a product relative to what they pay for it.

entries.title: Most Probable Value (MPV)
entries.formula: MPV = X̄ = ΣX/n = (X1 + X2 + X3 + ⋯ + Xn)/n
entries.variables: X = individual observations, n = number of observations
entries.description: The arithmetic mean of a set of repeated observations — the value with the greatest probability of being correct.

entries.title: Residual (Deviation)
entries.variables: X = a measured value, X̄ = most probable value (mean)
entries.description: Difference between any single measured value and the most probable value of the quantity.

entries.title: Probable Error of a Single Measurement of a Series
entries.variables: v = residual, n = number of observations
entries.description: Defines the range within which there is a 50% chance the true value of a single measurement lies.

entries.title: Probable Error of the Mean
entries.variables: v = residual, n = number of observations
entries.description: Defines the range within which there is a 50% chance the true value of the mean lies.

entries.title: Weight (Interrelationship of Errors)
entries.variables: PE = probable error of a measurement
entries.description: Relative reliability assigned to a measurement — inversely proportional to the square of its probable error.

entries.title: Summation of Errors
entries.variables: PE1...PEn = probable errors of individual quantities
entries.description: Probable error of a quantity computed as the sum of several independently measured quantities.

entries.title: Product of Errors
entries.variables: Q1, Q2 = measured quantities, PE1, PE2 = their probable errors
entries.description: Probable error of a quantity computed as the product of two independently measured quantities.

entries.title: Stadia Method Distance
entries.variables: K = stadia interval factor of the instrument, s = difference between upper and lower stadia hair readings, C = distance from the center of the instrument to the principal focus (instrument constant)
entries.description: Horizontal distance determined indirectly using a telescope's stadia hairs and a graduated rod.

entries.title: Subtense Bar Method Distance
entries.variables: s = length of the subtense bar, α = angle subtended by the targets
entries.description: Horizontal distance obtained directly (no slope correction needed) from a subtense bar and the horizontal angle it subtends.

entries.title: Slope Taping — Horizontal Distance
entries.formula: d = s cos α        d = √(s² − h²)
entries.variables: d = horizontal distance, s = slope distance, α = angle of inclination of the slope, h = difference in elevation
entries.description: Converts a tape measurement made along a uniform slope into an equivalent horizontal distance.

entries.title: Taping Correction — Incorrect Tape Length
entries.formula: Corr = TL − NL        C1 = Corr(ML/NL)        CL = ML ± C1
entries.variables: TL = true/actual length of tape, NL = nominal length of tape, ML = measured length, C1 = total correction, CL = corrected length
entries.description: Corrects a taped measurement when the tape's actual length differs from its nominal (labeled) length.

entries.title: Taping Correction — Slope
entries.formula: d = s − Ch        Gentle slope (<20%): Ch = h²/2s        Steep slope (20–30%): Ch = h²/2s + h⁴/8s³        Very steep slope (>30%): Ch = s(1 − cos θ)
entries.variables: s = slope distance, h = difference in elevation, θ = angle of inclination
entries.description: Correction subtracted from a slope-taped distance to obtain the horizontal distance, by slope steepness category.

entries.title: Taping Correction — Temperature
entries.variables: α = coefficient of linear expansion per degree (steel tape: 0.0000116/°C), L = length of tape measured, T = observed temperature, T0 = temperature at which the tape was standardized
entries.description: Corrects a taped measurement for thermal expansion or contraction of the tape.

entries.title: Taping Correction — Tension (Pull)
entries.variables: P = measured/applied pull, P0 = standard pull, L = length of tape measured, A = cross-sectional area of tape, E = modulus of elasticity, W = total weight of tape, γ = unit weight of tape (steel: γ=7.866×10⁻³ kg/cm³, A=0.02–0.06 cm², E=2.00–2.10×10⁶ kg/cm²)
entries.description: Corrects a taped measurement when the pull applied differs from the tape's standard pull.

entries.title: Taping Correction — Sag
entries.formula: C_s = w²L³/(24P²)        C_s = W²L/(24P²)        W² = w²L²
entries.variables: w = weight of tape per unit length, W = total weight of tape between supports, L = unsupported length of tape, P = pull/tension applied
entries.description: Corrects for the shortening of the horizontal distance caused by a tape sagging between supports.

entries.title: Normal Tension
entries.variables: P_N = normal tension/pull needed to eliminate sag effect, P_S = standard pull for the tape, W = total weight of tape between supports, A = cross-sectional area, E = modulus of elasticity
entries.description: The pull at which the tape's elongation exactly offsets the shortening caused by sag.

entries.title: Differential Leveling — Height of Instrument
entries.formula: HI = Elev + BS        Elev = HI − FS
entries.variables: HI = height of instrument (collimation), Elev = elevation of a point, BS = backsight reading, FS = foresight reading
entries.description: Basic leveling relations for determining elevations using backsight and foresight rod readings.

entries.title: Reciprocal Leveling
entries.variables: a, b = readings from one instrument setup, a', b' = readings from the reciprocal setup, TDE = true difference in elevation
entries.description: Determines the difference in elevation between two points across an obstacle by averaging readings from setups on each side.

entries.title: Trigonometric Leveling — Difference in Elevation
entries.formula: DE_ab = d tan α + HI − RR        DE_ab = s sin α + HI − RR
entries.variables: d = horizontal distance, s = slope distance, α = vertical angle, HI = height of instrument, RR = rod reading
entries.description: Computes the difference in elevation between two points using a measured angle and distance.

entries.title: Trigonometric Leveling — Curvature and Refraction Correction
entries.formula: DE_ab = d tan α + HI − RR ± 0.0675K²        DE_ab = s sin α + HI − RR ± 0.0675K²
entries.variables: K = horizontal distance in km, sign added for an upward sight and subtracted for a downward sight
entries.description: Trigonometric leveling elevation difference corrected for earth curvature and atmospheric refraction, used for sight distances exceeding 300 m.

entries.title: Trigonometric Leveling — Reciprocal Vertical-Angle Observation
entries.formula: DE_ab = (d/2)(tan α + tan β)        DE_ab = (s/2)(sin α + sin β)
entries.variables: α, β = vertical angles observed from each end of the line, d/s = horizontal/slope distance
entries.description: Eliminates the need for curvature/refraction correction by averaging reciprocal vertical-angle observations from both ends of the line.

entries.title: Altimeter Survey — Two-Base Method Ratio
entries.variables: S, S' = altimeter readings, L, L' = time intervals, H = elevation values at the two bases
entries.description: Relates readings between a low reference base and a high reference base to eliminate the need for temperature/humidity correction in altimeter surveys.

entries.title: Stadia Distance (Simplified)
entries.variables: k = stadia constant (typically 100), s = upper stadia hair reading − lower stadia hair reading
entries.description: Rapid indirect distance measurement using a telescope's stadia hairs and a graduated rod.
